### trick for extra sharing  {.smaller}


* sharing writeable data is fine --- until either process modifies it 

   * example: default value of global variables
   * might typically not change
   * (or OS might have preloaded executable's data anyways)

* can we detect modifications? 
<hr class="vspace" />
* trick: tell CPU (via page table) shared part is read-only
* processor will trigger a fault when it's written

### copy-on-write and page tables


::: {.r-stack .my-full}
![](/vm-fault/texfig/copyOnWrite-pt-only.figure-1.svg){.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="partial page table listing from VPNs 0x601 through 0x605. Each page is alloate to a different physical page and is valid and writeable."}

![](/vm-fault/texfig/copyOnWrite-pt-only.figure-2.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="Two copies of the same page table. Both the original and the copy has the same physical pages. Both have every page marked not writeable."}

![](/vm-fault/texfig/copyOnWrite-pt-only.figure-3.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3 fig-alt="the page table entry for page VPN 0x605 in the new page table is highlighted."}

![](/vm-fault/texfig/copyOnWrite-pt-only.figure-4.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=4 fig-alt="the new page table's entry for VPN 0x605 is modified to be writeable and have a different physical page number."}

:::

::: {.myoverbox .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2 .vlow}

copy operation actually duplicates page table <br />
both processes _share all physical pages_ <br />
but marked _read-only in both tables_

:::

::: {.myoverbox .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3 .vlow}

when either process tries to write a read-only page <br />
triggers a page fault --- OS actually copies the page

:::

::: {.myoverbox .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=4 .vlow}

after allocating a copy, OS reruns the write instruction

:::
